done_when: Every status, count and time on the board page and in forge board --json comes from one shared derivation, so they agree: stories the roadmap marks done count and show as done; items idle past the stalled threshold show as stalled with their idle time and what they wait on, and finished items never do; a running worker or review shows as running with its elapsed time; ready-to-merge, plan-read and waiting-for-approval stages match forge next; a finished story's parts show finished; prose and timeline times agree; header counts are labelled separately for stories and fixes; a person shows under one display name; titles are shortened at a word boundary; command tests reproduce each of these on a board with real-shaped data for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Functional. When a teammate updates a task name on the published story branch and starts that task, an observer with an older local story worktree gets contradictory names on the board. This lookup always selects the local story worktree, even when it is behind the published plan. The dependency map instead uses `story._plan` (board.py:574–575), whose published-plan reconciliation is implemented in story.py:455–477. Consequently, the task card and JSON child retain the old name while the dependency map shows the new one; `_page` also replaces its freshly gathered task name with this stale row title at board.py:1099. Use the same reconciled plan for both derivations.
findings.title: Derive task titles from the current published story plan

stop.reason: Owner wants every in-flight fix finished; narrowed to the three remaining findings: distinct test criterion numbers, unknown finish date for roadmap-done stories without completion evidence, a 25-hour stalled assertion

why: The forge board page shows wrong or contradicting data (Opus review of a real client board, 2026-10-09): stories the roadmap marks done show as 'Not started yet' and count as needing a spec; items idle for days aren't shown as stalled while finished stories are flagged stalled; running workers and reviews show as 'Needs fixes'; a card says Ready to merge while the header counts none; a story in a plan-read round shows as 'Waiting for approval'; a finished story's part says 'In progress'; prose times disagree with the timeline; header counts mix stories and fixes unlabelled; one person appears under two names; fix titles are cut mid-word
